data.narrative:
MacroFab, a Series C robotics and manufacturing platform founded by Chris Church, has raised $141M to date. The valuation analysis draws on two methodologies triangulated against a comp universe of nine private robotics firms and one public comparable (277810.KQ), selected for sector and stage alignment.

Stage-progression methodology applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yielding $240M. Peer-median methodology examines seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—including Exotec ($2.0B Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B Series D)—producing a median valuation of $1.6B with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. The wide disparity between methodologies reflects stage and performance variation within the peer set; comparables include both Series B and Series D companies, creating meaningful valuation spread.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $204M (low, stage-progression floor) to $1.9B (high, peer ceiling), with a median estimate of $945M. This $1.7B range reflects material uncertainty around MacroFab's relative positioning within the peer set on execution metrics and market capture. Narrowing this band would require visibility into revenue scale, unit economics, or capital efficiency relative to named comparables.
